suggestions.reason: The assertion as written fails because of leftover duplicate files from the execution process, not because the skill produced wrong content. A more discriminating assertion would be: 'Exactly 3 canonical post draft files produced (one per scheduled day, no duplicates per date)' — or the eval could be structured to check files in the official batch folder (04-gmb/posts/drafts/) rather than the eval outputs copy, where deduplication was not enforced. As written, the assertion can be gamed by simply not copying draft iterations to the outputs directory.

No assertion checks whether the CTA URLs are live/reachable. Post 3 uses https://75degreeac.com/ac-repair-houston-tx/ as the CTA for an HVAC installation/services post — there is a potential content-URL mismatch (repair URL for a symptom-guide post). An assertion checking CTA URL relevance to post content would catch this.

No assertion verifies that each post body is free of em dashes. The skill has an explicit em dash ban (they render as question marks in GBP), and the transcript notes Post 1's first draft had 3 em dashes that were caught and fixed. This is a high-value rule violation that goes unchecked by the current assertion set.

suggestions.assertion: Each post body is within 1200-1450 chars
suggestions.reason: The assertion is ambiguous about what 'post body' means when the file contains a compliance tag and a ## Research Notes section appended to ## Post Body. The grader must decide whether to measure the raw section or the publishable content. This ambiguity should be resolved: specify 'GBP-publishable body (excluding any metadata tags and Research Notes appended in the file)'.

eval_feedback.overall: The assertion set correctly identifies the two main failure modes of the old skill (duplicate files + embedded Research Notes). The 8 passing assertions are meaningful and mostly discriminating. Four improvement opportunities exist: CTA URL relevance, em dash checking, file count precision, and char count definition clarity.
